This file will go through the very basic step, with minimal cleaning.
It will also create 

I don't want to redownload each time I run this file (because it takes
time and is an unnecessary load on Project Gutenberg) . I can save a working copy of the data and use that
when experimenting.  Doing it this way I can still run the whole
process by deleting or renaming the "data/quakersaints.rda" file. 

To load the saved dataset I use the `load()` function.

```{r }
# If the file of saved data is not present
if (!file.exists(here("data/quakersaints.rda"))) {
     # download the data from Project Gutenberg
     quakersaints <-  gutenberg_download(c(19605))
     # and save it to that file name.
     save(quakersaints, file="data/quakersaints.rda")
# Otherwise, 
} else {
     # load the data set from the file.
     load(here("data/quakersaints.rda"))
}
```

I'm going to use blocks like this in almost all of my files. 
This gives me the flexibility I need.
I could make this into a function.  However, I instead chose to make
it a "code snippet" which will let me easily paste it in any markdown
file.
